judgment.judgment: Not the forced-seller story here because this registry supplies no spinoff evidence for the ticker. The parent, distribution date, distribution ratio, debt raised, cash sent to the parent and retained liabilities are all marked not applicable. With no distribution, there is no identifiable group of recipients who were handed shares they could not or would not hold. I cannot show index exclusion, a size mismatch against a parent, a missing dividend or a different business. The code therefore gives nothing for the forced-seller and indifferent-seller criteria, and I do not read more into them. The same applies to the load-pushed-in and parent-motive criteria: no parent and no transferred obligations are supplied, so there is nothing to quantify. Insider open-market purchases are a stated limitation, since no insider report was saved and coverage is not established. The one criterion with data is price against value, and it also fails. Owner cash flow is built from after-tax earnings [10-K.txt:L1204] section CONSOLIDATED STATEMENTS OF INCOME; year ended 2026-08-30; units 1e+06; NET INCOME = 9.226e+09, depreciation and amortization [10-K.txt:L1660] section CONSOLIDATED STATEMENTS OF CASH FLOWS; year ended 2026-08-30; units 1e+06; Depreciation and amortization = 2.674e+09 and capital spending [10-K.txt:L1708] section CONSOLIDATED STATEMENTS OF CASH FLOWS; year ended 2026-08-30; units 1e+06; Additions to property and equipment = -6.435e+09; spending = -(-6.435e+09) = 6.435e+09, and then divided over the share count [10-K.txt:L86] section Cover page; as of 2026-09-29; quote: The number of shares outstanding of the registrant’s common stock as of September 29, 2026, was 443,129,349. The supplied code comparison puts the market price far above even the low case, so the price is not below what the cash flow supports on this method. Cheapness caused by forced selling is not supported by anything supplied. The stock looks expensive against its own owner cash flow, not mispriced by a seller who does not care about value.
judgment.next_filing_trigger: If the cash flow statement in the next quarterly report shows owner cash flow, meaning after-tax earnings plus depreciation and amortization less additions to property and equipment, running at a pace many times the three-year average used in the low case, the price gap to the low case would narrow materially. Absent that, the price stays well above the low case and the spinoff-seller story still has no filing support.
judgment.insight: Capital spending is far larger than depreciation and amortization, so owner cash flow is a fraction of reported earnings; headline profit overstates what is left for owners.
